profile_text.body:
NVIDIA is a publicly traded semiconductor and computing company, founded in 1993 and headquartered in Santa Clara, CA. It reported revenue of $215,938,000,000 for the fiscal year ending January 25, 2026, and trades on public markets under the ticker NVDA. The company's AI work spans hardware platforms, inference infrastructure, and foundation models, with its site focused on positioning NVIDIA as a full-stack provider for enterprise agentic AI.

NVIDIA's Nemotron is described on its site as a family of multimodal, open AI models built for agentic workflows, covering reasoning, vision, speech, retrieval-augmented generation, and safety tasks. The site describes specific models including Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, targeted at faster specialized task completion, and NeMo Switchyard, described as a routing layer that directs agent steps to appropriate models. Nemotron models are published under the NVIDIA Open Model License, which the company describes as permissive and allowing commercial use and redistribution without attribution. NVIDIA also offers Nemotron through its NIM microservices, which are inference microservices for enterprise deployment requiring an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license, available through build.nvidia.com. The site mentions Bryan Catanzaro, VP of applied deep learning research at NVIDIA, as a spokesperson for the Nemotron initiative, and cites ServiceNow as a named ecosystem partner.

The held facts confirm NVIDIA maintains two tracked AI products, Nemotron and NIM, and that the company holds SEC filing CIK 0001045810 with a 10-K on record. No litigation or MCP server registrations are noted in the held data.
